# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: what the shaper is, which roles do
the work, and what should change. A shaper is always set (`shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`, never `null`), but it need not be an LLM: keep the orchestrator,
or replace it with a script role (a decision tree, a state machine, a fixed rule) or
anything else the evidence shows advances the project best per unit of quota. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

After a wake or recovery, check the current iteration's recorded orders and their
results before restoring a saved task graph. Missing `.session/` files do not show
that orders were never consumed. Read completed audit outputs before deciding the
next action. Do not submit the same audit again without a new evidence question
and a stated expected gain. A recovery copy is historical evidence, not a queue.
When no new policy task is needed, write `{"wake": false, "tasks": []}` to
`.session/orders.json` and return ordinary work to the shaper. If current order
state is unavailable, preserve the uncertainty instead of blindly replaying orders.

## Write for the owner in Simplified Technical English

Write each text that the owner reads in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: the
`title`, `what`, `why` and `unblocks` of each request in `.session/requests.json`, and
`.session/report.md`. The owner must understand the text at first reading, without the
context of your session.

- Use short sentences: at most 20 words in an instruction, 25 in a description.
- Use one idea in one sentence. Use the active voice and the simple present or past tense.
- Use the approved meaning of a word. Use the same word for the same thing every time;
  do not use a synonym. Use the terms of `CONTEXT.md` (for example Owner request,
  Policymaker, Goal gate) and explain no other special term without a concrete example.
- Put the decision first: what the owner must do, or what the owner must decide, then
  the reason. A request has this order: `title` (the action), `what` (the situation and
  the action), `why`, `unblocks` (what starts when the owner acts).
- Write the steps for the owner as a numbered list. One step is one action. Give the
  exact file, command or value.
- Keep the structure and the formatting: headings, lists, and tables stay. Do not make
  the text longer, and do not remove a fact or a link to evidence. Remove only words
  that carry no information.

Do not change `frozen`, `readiness` and `test`. They are exact content that the engine
applies or runs. Do not change a quotation of evidence.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

"""What a session receives as its state and its searchable history. The engine runs this in the tokenless job
(`python3 session-state.py facts.json`) when it stages a session, and prints nothing else: one JSON object
{"loop_state": <object or null>, "files": {"history/<path>": "<text>"}}. The engine writes `loop_state` to
`.session/loop-state.json` and the files under `.session/`, after checking paths and sizes. An invalid answer fails the
iteration and rolls `policy/` back.

facts.json: role, state (the Policymaker/shaper snapshot the engine stored, already limited to what the role may see; null
for other roles), full (the whole history, or only what the task selected), checkout, records (iteration records), reports
(report snapshots: {issue, source, snapshot, body}), outboxes (the raw `.session/suggestions.json` of each session: {issue, raw}).

Suggestions are handled here. A session proposes `[{"kind","what","why","evidence"}]`; the Policymaker decides them in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json`, {"<id>": {"status": "handled" | "rejected", "reason": "..."}}; the rest stay pending in
`loop_state["suggestions"]`, with the diagnostics of the entries that were refused in `loop_state["suggestion_diagnostics"]`.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys

facts = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
full = bool(facts.get("full"))
files, tasks, snapshots, age = {}, {}, {}, {}


def field(body, key):
    for line in body.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(key + ":"):
            return line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    return ""


# The engine refuses an answer over 8 MiB (characters), and the whole history grows with every iteration; so the answer is
# kept compact and bounded. Records older than KEEP_INPUT_STATE iterations lose `input_state` (the goal, parameters and
# request lists repeated in every record; ~half of all record bytes, still in iterations/<n>.json of the checkout), and,
# if the answer still exceeds BUDGET, the oldest history files are left out and counted in the manifest.
KEEP_INPUT_STATE = 20
BUDGET = 6 * 1024 * 1024


def dump(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))


newest = max([r["iteration"] for r in facts.get("records", [])] or [0])
for record in facts.get("records", []):
    n = record["iteration"]
    if n <= newest - KEEP_INPUT_STATE and "input_state" in record:
        record = dict(record, input_state="omitted from older records; read iterations/%04d.json" % n)
    files["history/records/%04d.json" % n] = dump(record) + "\n"
    age["history/records/%04d.json" % n] = n
    for task in record.get("tasks", []):
        if type(task.get("issue")) is int:
            tasks[task["issue"]] = dict(task, iteration=n)
    for session in record.get("outcome", {}).get("sessions", []):
        tasks[session["issue"]] = dict(tasks.get(session["issue"], {}), **session, iteration=n)

# Identity, not a mutable "latest" alias, names a report body; the last copy of an identity wins.
for report in facts.get("reports", []):
    snapshots[(report["issue"], report["snapshot"])] = report

for (issue, snapshot), report in snapshots.items():
    task = tasks.setdefault(issue, {"issue": issue, "title": "Session #%s" % issue})
    body = report["body"]
    header = ("# Session #%s\nTask: %s\nRole: %s\nIteration: %s\nStatus: %s\nVerdict: %s\nSource: %s\nSnapshot: %s\n\n" %
              (issue, str(task.get("title", "")).replace("\n", " "), task.get("role", ""), task.get("iteration"),
               field(body, "status") or task.get("status", ""), field(body, "verdict") or task.get("verdict", ""),
               report["source"], snapshot))
    files["history/sessions/%s/%s.md" % (issue, snapshot)] = header + body
    age["history/sessions/%s/%s.md" % (issue, snapshot)] = task.get("iteration") or 0
latest = {issue: {"issue": issue, "source": r["source"], "snapshot": snapshot}
          for (issue, snapshot), r in snapshots.items()}
for issue, task in tasks.items():
    detail = {key: value for key, value in task.items() if key != "body"}
    files["history/sessions/%s/task.md" % issue] = ("# Session #%s task and result\n\n```json\n%s\n```\n\n%s\n" %
                                                    (issue, dump(detail), task.get("body", "")))
    age["history/sessions/%s/task.md" % issue] = task.get("iteration") or 0

def suggestions():
    try:
        decided = json.load(open("policy/suggestion-decisions.json", encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        decided = {}
    pending, diagnostics = [], []
    for outbox in facts.get("outboxes", []):
        issue = outbox["issue"]
        try:
            items = json.loads(outbox["raw"])
            if not isinstance(items, list) or len(items) > 100:
                raise ValueError("an array of at most 100 objects")
        except ValueError:
            diagnostics.append("session #%s: suggestions.json must be an array of at most 100 objects" % issue)
            continue
        report = latest.get(issue)
        for index, item in enumerate(items):
            fields = ("kind", "what", "why", "evidence")
            if (not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != set(fields)
                    or any(not isinstance(item[k], str) or not item[k].strip() or len(item[k]) > 20000 for k in fields)
                    or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}", item["kind"])):
                diagnostics.append("session #%s: suggestions.json item %s needs kind (lowercase words and hyphens), what, why "
                                   "and evidence strings" % (issue, index))
                continue
            key = "suggestion-" + hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([issue, item], sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
            if key not in decided:
                pending.append(dict(item, id=key, status="pending", source=report))
    return pending, diagnostics


# Leave out the oldest history files until the answer fits the budget (the engine's own limit is 8 MiB).
omitted = 0
size = sum(len(path) + len(text) for path, text in files.items())
for path in sorted(files, key=lambda p: (age.get(p, 0), p)):
    if size <= BUDGET:
        break
    size -= len(path) + len(files.pop(path))
    omitted += 1

scope = "all permitted history in the prepared checkout" if full else "task-selected inputs"
manifest = {"scope": scope, "checkout": facts.get("checkout"), "records": len(facts.get("records", [])),
            "report_snapshots": len(snapshots), "omitted_oldest_files": omitted,
            "paths": {"records": "records/<iteration>.json", "sessions": "sessions/<issue>/"},
            "search": "Search Session titles, roles, outcomes and report text; read selected files. "
                      "No match does not establish that work was never attempted. "
                      "Current report references and pinned evidence are distinguished in ../reports/index.json."}
files["history/manifest.json"] = json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + "\n"

loop_state = None
if isinstance(facts.get("state"), dict):
    state = facts["state"]
    # The previous outcome is current context; the rest is discoverable history.
    loop_state = dict(state, iterations=state.get("iterations", [])[-1:],
                      history={"manifest": ".session/history/manifest.json", "records": manifest["records"],
                               "report_snapshots": len(snapshots), "scope": scope})
    if facts.get("role") == "policymaker":      # execution roles are not shown them
        loop_state["suggestions"], loop_state["suggestion_diagnostics"] = suggestions()
# Characters are what the engine counts; write UTF-8 bytes directly so the locale cannot break a Polish text.
sys.stdout.buffer.write(json.dumps({"loop_state": loop_state, "files": files}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regression check for iteration 0161: policy/session-state.py must print at most 8 MiB (bytes) even when the history
is JSON-heavy (quotes double when a record is embedded as a JSON string) and holds Polish text (2 UTF-8 bytes per letter).
Run from the repository root: python3 policy/checks/session_state_size.py"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

LIMIT = 8 * 1024 * 1024
heavy = {"k%d" % i: "\"ąęłóśżź\"" * 40 for i in range(60)}           # quote- and Polish-heavy payload
records = [{"iteration": n, "tasks": [{"issue": 1000 + n, "title": "zadanie ż"}], "input_state": heavy,
            "outcome": {"sessions": [{"issue": 1000 + n, "status": "done"}]}} for n in range(1, 400)]
reports = [{"issue": 1000 + n, "source": "s", "snapshot": "x%d" % n, "body": "status: done\n" + "„łóż” \"q\" " * 4000}
           for n in range(1, 400)]
facts = {"role": "policymaker", "state": {"iterations": [{"n": 1}], "goal": {"text": "Cel ąę" * 2000}},
         "full": True, "checkout": "c", "records": records, "reports": reports, "outboxes": []}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "facts.json")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(facts, handle, ensure_ascii=False)
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "policy/session-state.py", path], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
answer = json.loads(out.decode("utf-8"))
manifest = json.loads(answer["files"]["history/manifest.json"])
print("printed bytes %d, characters %d, files %d, omitted %d" %
      (len(out), len(out.decode("utf-8")), len(answer["files"]), manifest["omitted_oldest_files"]))
assert len(out) <= LIMIT, "answer exceeds 8 MiB"
assert manifest["omitted_oldest_files"] > 0, "test input did not exercise the budget"
assert "history/records/0399.json" in answer["files"], "newest record was dropped"
assert answer["loop_state"]["history"]["records"] == len(records)
print("OK")

# Policymaker #729, iteration 0162

Trigger: iteration 0161 failed. The engine refused the output of `policy/session-state.py` because it was more than 8,388,608 bytes. The engine then rolled back `policy/`.

## Cause

- The size limit in the script counted characters of each history path and text. The limit was 6 MiB.
- The engine counts the printed answer. Each history file is a JSON string in that answer. A record is JSON inside a JSON string, so each quote mark gets an escape character.
- Polish letters use 2 UTF-8 bytes each.
- The script did not count `loop_state`.
- With 198 records and 803 report snapshots, the printed bytes went above 8 MiB. The character count stayed below 6 MiB.

## Change

- `policy/session-state.py` now gives each file a size in printed bytes (`json.dumps`, then UTF-8). It subtracts the printed `loop_state` and keeps 64 KiB free. Then it removes the oldest history files until the answer fits.
- New regression check: `policy/checks/session_state_size.py`. It uses synthetic history with many quotes and much Polish text. Result: 6,218,178 printed bytes, 996 oldest files removed, newest record kept, `OK`.
- `.session/orders.json` is `{"wake": false, "tasks": []}`. Ordinary work goes back to the Shaper.
- `policy/working-memory.md` has the new entry.

## Expected gain and check

Expected gain: iteration 0163 stages sessions again, and the size limit does not fail again.
Check: the next record does not fail because of the size of the session-state output. `history/manifest.json` shows `omitted_oldest_files`. When an old history file is missing, read `iterations/<n>.json` in the checkout.

- Saved work: the script fix and the check are in `policy/`. I tested the script only with synthetic data. I did not test it with the real engine facts.
